title: Talking through the maximum subarray instead of going quiet
takeaway: Interviewers cannot evaluate a candidate who does not talk; restate, clarify, agree the approach, ask when stuck, then trace.
sources: Most candidates fail communication, not problem-solving.
Do not start coding without buy-in.
Getting a hint does not disqualify you - staying silent for 10 minutes does.

turns.text: So to make sure I understand - I need to find the maximum sum subarray. Is that right?
turns.note: Restating lets the interviewer correct you early

turns.text: Can the array be empty? What should I return in that case?
turns.note: Clarifying questions earn credit for edge cases

turns.text: Brute force is O(n²). I think dynamic programming gives O(n) time. Does that approach make sense before I code it?
turns.note: State the approach and wait for confirmation

turns.text: I am a little stuck on this part. Can I talk through what I am thinking?
turns.note: Interviewers almost always give hints when asked
Catching your own bugs beats having them pointed out
